newsitem.title: UK: Clean tankers show firm tone on lack of tonnage.
newsitem.headline: Clean tankers show firm tone on lack of tonnage.

text.p: The clean tanker market had a reasonably firm tone this week, benefiting from a lack of suitable tonnage rather than strong enquiry, brokers said on Friday.

Mediterranean rates fell early in the week, but interest arose in shipping product east as an arbitrage window opened up. Some product also moved from the Baltic, with the Santa Lucia reported fixed with 50,000 tonnes of gas oil from Ventspils to Singapore for $1.3 million for Greenenergy.
Some brokers said Med/east fixtures had been limited by a lack of tonnage.

Brokers E.A. Gibson said that although "this year has so far been encouraging for owners of product carriers, ...make no mistake, there could be some tough times ahead, as was the case last year, particularly during the summer months."

They said longer haul cargoes in the Middle East fared slightly better than medium haul vessels as modern tonnage was in demand. Cargoes of 31,500 tonnes were being fixed from the Red Sea to Japan at W220.
They also said a lack of interest in larger medium range cargoes in the east has again forced owners to ballast towards the Mediterranean in search of employment.

The volatile Caribbean market fell to about W285 after reaching W310 last week, while there was interest in combining stems in the inter-U.K./Cont sector and in shipping product transatlantic at about W200 and to the Far East.
But Gibson said owners of 70,000-80,000 tonne vessels were demanding more than $2 million for Singapore cargoes, and this was becoming unworkable.
